lesson.summary: Introduction to C: History, Characteristics and Classification
points: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s, building on B in the Unix environment.
C is general purpose, procedural and imperative; it is normally compiled.
Portability needs care with implementation-dependent behavior. Middle-level is an informal classroom label, not an ISO language category.

archive_evidence.history: Ritchie built a B cross-compiler that ran on a smaller computer but emitted machine instructions for a GE-635 mainframe.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: In B, the same operator could mean a bitwise operation or control how a condition was evaluated, depending on where it appeared.
archive_evidence.source: Dennis Ritchie, The Development of the C Language

archive_evidence.history: C is normally compiled. Write the source, translate it and link it as needed, then run the resulting program. Tests check whether its behavior matches the goal after compilation succeeds.
archive_evidence.source: GNU Compiler Collection Manual, Overall Options

archive_evidence.era: A clean build and a test run
archive_evidence.history: Treat build diagnostics and program output as different clues. A successful build and a correct result are separate milestones.
archive_evidence.source: GNU Compiler Collection Manual, Overall Options

archive_evidence.history: Preprocessing, compilation, assembly and linking are stages a compiler driver can coordinate. A linked executable can then be run on its target.
archive_evidence.source: GNU Compiler Collection Manual, Overall Options
